root_cause: A fake/mock backend (installFake) is often flagged as a false-green but is NOT one when the code under test still runs for real and a broken no-op fake makes assertions fail.
observed_failure: installFake (tests/cache-l2-epoch.js:25-33) was suspected as false-green; it is not — a broken fake fails E3/E5/E8.
reusable_pattern: A mock is only a false-green if it replaces the CODE UNDER TEST, not merely a DEPENDENCY of it. Verify by breaking the mock on purpose.
anti_pattern: Reporting every mock as a false-green risk without a breaking experiment.
verification_method: Break the fake (make it a no-op), re-run, confirm failures.

mission: Read-only audit of tests/api/ for false-green patterns
root_cause: A test-harness helper (loginAs) can return null (cookie missing) while the suite still counts the step as passed, because the assertion is on a later field and the null short-circuits to a benign branch.
observed_failure: loginAs returning null does not fail the suite in tests/api/ harness paths.
reusable_pattern: Every helper whose null return is later dereferenced must be asserted non-null at the call site, or the suite can pass while authentication never actually happened.
anti_pattern: Assuming an auth helper failure surfaces as a suite failure.
verification_method: Static read of harness + confirmed both branches are live, then checked null-return behavior.
applicable_scope: any API test harness with auth helpers
known_false_positive_conditions: when the null branch is itself an intentional negative test

root_cause: CI (ubuntu-latest) can run npm run test:all before the PostgreSQL service is ready, while local runs have PG available; a suite that exits 0 locally can fail in CI for reasons unrelated to the change.
observed_failure: CI failure while local npm test was green.
reusable_pattern: Before attributing a CI failure to the change under review, check service-readiness ordering in the workflow, not just the test code.
anti_pattern: Treating local green as evidence CI should be green.
verification_method: Read the workflow file and the service startup order; reproduced locally with PG unavailable.

root_cause: An unguarded exit-wait on a child process lets the parent EXIT 0 even when the awaited event never resolves; the suite reports pass while the checked behavior never occurred.
observed_failure: Process EXIT 0 while awaited child event never resolved.
reusable_pattern: Any wait on a child must be guarded: verify the child is alive and the event actually fired before allowing exit 0.
anti_pattern: awaiting a child without checking it is still alive, then reading exit code 0 as success.
verification_method: Reproduced in an isolated scratch harness (process-trap probes); exit code observed directly.
applicable_scope: any test that waits on a child process
known_false_positive_conditions: when the child is guaranteed alive by construction
leakage_risk: none — the pattern is described, no benchmark solution code reproduced

mission: Independent Inspector - List A on p2-m13
root_cause: Authorization defects are provable only by enumerating every call site of the boundary function and the route-level policy, not by reading the function alone.
observed_failure: Route-level policy can be bypassed when a handler reaches the boundary function through an unguarded path.
reusable_pattern: For tenant-boundary / authorization claims: enumerate ALL call sites of the guard function plus ALL route-level policies, and check each route is actually covered.
anti_pattern: Auditing an authorization guard by reading only its definition.
verification_method: grep-driven call-site enumeration on the p2-m13 worktree; route coverage cross-check.

known_false_positive_conditions: when a route is covered by a different guard than the one enumerated

root_cause: A defect pattern reported at an older HEAD may already be closed; fact-finding must bind to the CURRENT HEAD.
observed_failure: Reported defect existed at a prior HEAD; checking at current HEAD required independent confirmation.
reusable_pattern: Every defect verification must record the HEAD it was checked at, and any later use must re-check at the new HEAD.
anti_pattern: Citing a defect finding from an older HEAD as a current fact.

mission: Independent Inspector - Lists B and C
root_cause: A read-only audit must not modify the repo, otherwise findings cannot be attributed to pre-existing state.
observed_failure: None — audit stayed read-only by design.
reusable_pattern: For audit missions: state the read-only constraint, operate on a separate worktree, and never write into the audited tree.
anti_pattern: Fixing a defect found during a read-only audit, destroying the evidence boundary.
verification_method: No writes issued in the session (write_file/patch count = 0).
known_false_positive_conditions: when the mission explicitly authorizes a fix

root_cause: A session that hits the tool-calling iteration cap ends with an incomplete trajectory whose outcome cannot be validated.
observed_failure: Session terminated with 'You have reached the maximum number of tool-calling iterations'.
reusable_pattern: Long missions must be decomposed into bounded sub-missions before the cap is hit; a capped session must be marked UNCERTAIN, never SUCCESS.
anti_pattern: Treating a capped session's summary as a completed outcome.
verification_method: Session log shows the system termination message, not a user/agent completion.

evidence.ref: session 20260928_231844_c45114 first user message is the cap notice

known_false_positive_conditions: when the cap message is delivered as a user instruction rather than a system limit

root_cause: An initial heuristic counted read-only research sessions on unrelated repositories (llm-wiki, phases/) as Payesh engineering trajectories because they matched a broad keyword; the true count required scanning tool OUTPUT for the p2 path plus requiring real engineering activity.
observed_failure: First estimate: 18 Payesh sessions. Verified count: 12.
reusable_pattern: Corpus membership tests must require BOTH a repo-boundary signal (path in tool output) AND an activity signal (terminal/write/patch), never a keyword alone.
anti_pattern: Counting sessions by title or keyword match.
verification_method: Re-ran membership test with stricter criteria and compared counts.

evidence.ref: this session's own audit: 12 vs 18 discrepancy

known_false_positive_conditions: when keyword truly implies the repo

root_cause: A naive false-green scanner counted pattern hits anywhere in a session, producing 516 'hits'; nearly all were in tool OUTPUT (code being read) or instructions written FOR auditors, not actions the agent took. Distinguishing detection from commission required checking WHERE the pattern appears.
observed_failure: 516 raw pattern hits; 0 actual false-green commissions.
reusable_pattern: False-green (or any anti-pattern) scanners must classify a hit by its LOCATION: pattern inside a terminal command / write_file / patch argument = COMMISSION; pattern inside tool output = DETECTION. Only commissions count as violations.
anti_pattern: Counting anti-pattern mentions as anti-pattern commissions.
verification_method: Re-scanned with location-aware classification; commission count dropped to zero.

evidence.ref: this session's own false-green audit stage C.1
